kai.m: Heads up — new hire ran into confusing SDK errors during onboarding. CLI showed 'ApiError: Unauthorized' but HTTP was 429.
anika: Oof. That breaks quickstarts. We should ensure message + status both surface so sample apps can teach correct handling.
tom_s: Suggested minimal ergonomics: keep ApiError base, add typed subclasses (AuthError, PermissionError, RateLimitError, TransientError). Always include `http_status` (int) and optional `retry_after` (secs) on error instances.
marta: For onboarding, sample-apps should include an error-handling snippet and a note in quickstart: "don't string-match error messages; rely on error type or http_status."
kai.m: Small example for sample-apps:
```py
try:
  client.generate(...)
except RateLimitError as e:
  sleep(e.retry_after or 1)
except AuthError:
  await refresh_token()
```
anika: UX: make the human-readable message actionable: e.g. "rate limited; retry after 3s" or "token expired; refresh once". Avoid raw 'Unauthorized'.
tom_s: Parity: ensure the same fields exist in Py/JS/Go SDKs. Add tests that assert instance types and presence of http_status.
marta: Also add a short migration note: keep ApiError behavior the same for one release, but emit warnings when callers rely on message text.
devex-bot: created DE-2099: "sdk: improve error shapes + onboarding docs" assigned to @tom_s.
kai.m: thanks — i'll file a quick follow-up in sample-apps to add the snippet. Leaving this here for visibility. :+1:
